title: The three layer bands
takeaway: The paper divides the model's depth into three functional regions: an early sensory band where the J-space carries essentially no meaningful content, a middle workspace band (roughly L38 to L92 in Sonnet 4.5) where it holds persistent abstract content, and a late motor band where its vectors align with the imminent output token.
walkthrough:
This figure is a schematic, not a data plot. It draws the model's stack of layers as a single strip and colors it into the three [[layer-bands]] the paper has been arguing for: sensory at the bottom, workspace in the middle, motor at the top.

The layer numbers use the paper's percentage convention. Results are reported on 25 evenly spaced layers of the [[residual-stream]], reindexed to the range 0 to 100, so a layer number reads as a fraction of the model's depth ([[layer-percentage-indexing]]). The default model behind these numbers is Claude Sonnet 4.5, from the [[claude-model-family]].

Each band is defined by what the [[jacobian-lens]] finds there. In the [[sensory-layers]], roughly the first third of depth up to about L38, lens readouts are noisy and the [[j-space]] is close to empty: readout kurtosis sits near zero, and the lens vectors collapse into a small linear subspace. The first layer can only encode the identity of the current token, so this emptiness is expected at the very start. In the [[workspace-layers]], from about L38 to about L92, the J-space carries content that is abstract, persists across nearby token positions, and is distinct from both the input tokens and the next output token. This is the band in which all of the paper's workspace-like properties were demonstrated. In the [[motor-layers]], the final few layers past about L92, the lens readout snaps onto the model's actual next-token prediction. The paper reads these late vectors as representations that drive the imminent output rather than intermediate computations available for further use.

The boundaries come from converging evidence rather than from this drawing. A [[cka]] comparison of lens vectors across layer pairs shows an early block, a long middle block, and a small late block, and four [[workspace-boundary-metrics]] locate the same two transitions.

The division is cleaner in the figure than in the data. The paper notes that in some models the transitions are gradual, sometimes with sub-blocks, and that layer subsampling exaggerates the sharpness. It also concedes that the metrics are all derived from the J-lens itself, so an early-layer workspace the lens cannot resolve remains possible.

terms.definition: The paper's label for roughly the first third of the model's layers, up to about L38, where J-lens readouts are noisy and the J-space carries essentially no meaningful content.

The middle band of layers, roughly L38 to L92 in Sonnet 4.5, where the J-space holds persistent abstract content distinct from both the input tokens and the imminent output; the region where the workspace-like properties hold.

The final few layers, past about L92, where J-lens vectors align with the model's actual next-token prediction; the paper reads these as representations that drive the imminent output rather than intermediate computations.

The three bands are defined by what the J-space does in them, not by any architectural difference; every layer has the same transformer structure, and the division comes from lens-derived measurements.
Depth positions in the model's residual stream, reported on 25 evenly spaced layers reindexed to 0-100 so that a layer number reads as a percentage of total depth.
The set of activation-space points expressible as a sparse nonnegative combination of J-lens vectors; the candidate workspace whose per-band behavior this figure summarizes.

numbers.meaning: The workspace onset, about a third of the way through the model's depth. Below it, readout kurtosis is near zero, top-1 autocorrelation sits at the null, and the lens vectors span only a small subspace; all four boundary metrics rise around this layer.

The workspace end, shortly before the output. Past it, the lens's next-token accuracy jumps steeply and readouts converge on the model's actual prediction, which the paper takes as the switch from intermediate content to motor representations.
The reindexed layer scale: layer numbers are percentages of depth, so the same bands can be compared across models of different sizes.
The number of evenly spaced residual-stream layers actually sampled for all reported results; the paper notes this subsampling exaggerates how sharp the band transitions look.
The number of functional regions. The count comes from the block structure of the CKA layer-similarity matrix: one early block, one long middle block, one small late block.
